journey.name: Unsplash API key — bring your own, and the redirect that asks for it
journey.description:
Web image search runs on the user's own Unsplash access key, kept in the platform keystore. A build-time key (UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY in local.properties) is a fallback behind it, so the "no key at all" path needs that line blanked and the app rebuilt.
No key is ever displayed: the built-in one is only admitted to exist, and a saved one shows as its last four characters. Settings sets FLAG_SECURE on release builds, so `adb shell screencap` there returns a black frame — debug is exempt so this journey can screenshot. Requires a signed-in session (run journey 01).

actions.action: Launch the Loopky app and verify the Home screen is shown
Tap the element with resource-id "tab_profile", then the element with resource-id "profile_settings"

With UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY set in local.properties: verify the IMAGE SEARCH section shows "Unsplash access key" reading "Using Loopky's shared key (limited)", and verify the key itself appears nowhere in the layout dump
Tap the element with resource-id "settings_unsplash_key_edit", tap the field with resource-id "settings_unsplash_key_input", and type "not-a-real-key-1234"
Verify the field renders as bullet characters rather than the typed text, in the layout dump as well as on screen
Scroll down so the Save button is above the keyboard, then tap the element with resource-id "settings_unsplash_key_save"

Verify the element with resource-id "settings_unsplash_key_error" appears reading that Unsplash rejected the key, and that the status line still reads "Using Loopky's shared key" — the rejected key must not have been stored
Clear the field, type a valid Unsplash access key, and tap "settings_unsplash_key_save"
Verify the editor closes and the status line reads "Key set · ••••" followed by exactly four characters, and that the full key appears nowhere in the layout dump
Tap the element with resource-id "settings_unsplash_key_remove" and verify the status reverts to "Using Loopky's shared key (limited)"
Blank UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY in local.properties, rebuild and reinstall, then return to Settings and verify the status reads "Not set — web image search is off"
Tap "tab_decks", open any deck, tap "deck_edit", then tap the element with resource-id "deck_editor_cover"

Verify the sheet shows the element with resource-id "image_sheet_key_panel" explaining that web image search needs an Unsplash API key, with buttons "image_sheet_get_key" and "image_sheet_add_key", and that "image_pick_gallery" is still available — the gallery path works without a key
Tap "image_sheet_get_key" and verify a browser opens https://unsplash.com/oauth/applications; go back

Tap the element with resource-id "image_sheet_add_key" and verify the sheet dismisses and Settings opens scrolled to the Unsplash row, with "settings_unsplash_key_input" already expanded and focused (keyboard up)
Type a valid access key, tap "settings_unsplash_key_save", go back to the deck editor and reopen the cover sheet
Verify the panel is gone and the element with resource-id "image_grid" populates with cells

Release-build check: build and install a release APK, open Settings, run `adb shell screencap` and verify the resulting image is entirely black while `android layout` still reports the Settings content; leave Settings and verify screencap works again
